layers.name: Now
layers.is: What the game on main (2.82.0) does today. A loop the plan has and the game lacks shows as a ghost.

layers.name: Planned
layers.is: What Garrett has decided and the roadmap or design docs settle: the dice rework (3 AP and 1 chosen element), the atlas journey, three-pilot squads, the dossier. Where the plan says nothing, it is a hole.

layers.name: Proposed
layers.is: The plan plus this review's proposals (the 22 keywords, the three lines, combos per pilot). Every hole is filled with an invention, marked as one, for Garrett and Shombith to accept, change or throw out.

tiers.is: One touch and the game's answer: hover a face and see its numbers, pick a die, watch an intent arrow.
tiers.ask: Does the board answer before I commit?

tiers.is: One face played, from choosing it to its card going onto the track and coming home.
tiers.ask: Is the payoff worth the AP and the etherion, and do I see it land?

tiers.is: Faces chained in one turn, or across two pilots (a duet). The loops a kit has baked in.
tiers.ask: Does one face set up the next?

tiers.is: One round: intents shown, dice rolled, both pilots act, foes carry out what they said, the round ends. The kit pointed at the objective.
tiers.ask: Is the round a puzzle I can read and solve?

tiers.is: One objective on one atlas page, about 8 to 14 rounds, won or lost.
tiers.ask: Can I tell who is winning and why, and was the page part of it?

tiers.is: A run: draft, the route of seven rows, havens and events, the Heart at the end. One or more sittings.
tiers.ask: Do I want one more stop, and do I care where the route goes?

tiers.is: What a person keeps between expeditions: made pilots and their growth, canon notes, friends to play with.
tiers.ask: What do I have tomorrow that I did not have today?

tiers.is: What changes without you: new releases, new atlas pages, approved canon, storytellers, the way on to Cosmic Shore.

drivers.name: Puzzle
drivers.is: Reading the telegraphed board and finding the answer: the Into-the-Breach pleasure.

drivers.name: Mastery
drivers.is: Getting better: a cleaner turn, a harder wind, a bonus goal.

drivers.name: Toys
drivers.is: Combining keywords into something neither does alone: a push into a Field, a Link onto a Brute.

drivers.name: Big hit
drivers.is: The release of a payoff that took setting up.

drivers.name: Fellowship
drivers.is: Playing with and for a partner: duets, one pilot each, the table.

drivers.name: Discovery
drivers.is: Something new: a trait, a page, a foe, a stop you have not seen.

drivers.name: Collection
drivers.is: Having it: made pilots, their traits, gear.

drivers.name: Stakes
drivers.is: Something can be lost: a pilot downed, the Lifeline, the run.

drivers.name: Story
drivers.is: A pilot's voice, a place's field notes, the Terminal's log, canon you wrote.

drivers.name: Authorship
drivers.is: Making something that stays: a pilot, a backstory, a canon note.

drivers.name: Objective
drivers.is: The objective, the clock and the bonus goals a mission lays out.

drivers.name: Reward
drivers.is: Upgrade points, crystals, a trait offer: what a stop hands over.

handoffs.name: Bank full
handoffs.is: Etherions or points were banked, so you go and spend them one tier up: a big face, a Train.

handoffs.name: Objective met
handoffs.is: The loop's goal is reached and the tier above takes its next step.

handoffs.name: Loss
handoffs.is: A pilot is downed, a mission lost, a run ended: the tier above resets or sends you home.

handoffs.name: Reward to spend
handoffs.is: You hold something only useful in another loop: points, crystals, a trait offer.

handoffs.name: Something new
handoffs.is: A new trait, page, foe or release opens a loop you have not run.

handoffs.name: A friend
handoffs.is: An online game in the lobby or a friend at the table moves you to where they are.

handoffs.name: Enough of this
handoffs.is: The loop has stopped paying and you look for another at the same tier.

nodes.name: The long game
nodes.is: Everything Tumult offers a person over months. Both jobs live here; a good game to replay, and a workshop where Froglet's pilots and their stories get made.

phases.d: Something pulled you in: a friend in the lobby, a new release, a pilot you made last week.
The title screen offers a new expedition, Continue, games to join, the Atlas and your pilots.
Draft or bring a pilot, ride the route, face the Heart.
The pilot's traits and level, canon notes written, the pages you saw.
A release changes the rules, new pages and traits arrive, approved canon goes to the storytellers.

now.note: Releases come often (2.82.0 on 2026-11-20) and made pilots keep their growth since 2.76, but nothing in the game tells a returning player what changed or what is waiting for them.

plan.note: A run becomes a journey across atlas pages joined by a story; the web game gathers canon for AI storytellers; a finished dossier is a pilot ready for Cosmic Shore.

prop.note: Give the last phase a voice. The title shows what changed since you last flew, in keywords you already know.

holes.q: How often a person comes back, and how many expeditions they fly a week, is not measured.
holes.fill: Count expeditions started and finished per device and per online game (Froglet Analytics, web build only).

nodes.name: A sitting
nodes.is: One time you open the page. The title screen is the hub, and every change of place passes through it.

phases.d: New expedition, Continue, the lobby, Atlas, Codex, Canon.
One to five players; pre-made, made or drafted pilots.
The expedition, to the Heart or to a loss.
Win or lose text, the pilot comes home with what it earned.

now.note: Title, Continue mid-round, online lobby (2.80), Atlas, Codex and canon marks are all in.

holes.q: The ending sends you back to the title. Nothing offers the next step that fits what just happened.
holes.fill: The breath (new loop): after an expedition, one offered next step chosen from it: fly the same pilot again on the Gale, open the page it lost on in the Atlas, answer one canon question about that pilot.

nodes.name: The breath
nodes.is: Proposed. The pause after an expedition, treated as a loop of its own, where the game hands you up, down or across.

phases.d: Stops cleared, the faces that decided them, what the pilot gained.
A canon prompt about the moment that mattered, never a blank form.
The same pilot on a harder wind, or the page it lost on.

phases.n: Take it or go to the title

prop.note: Proposal P6. The canon prompts and the playtest report already know what happened; this adds the hand-off.

nodes.name: An expedition
nodes.is: A run: a squad of guides crosses land, sea and air along one route to the Heart. Saved at every node and every action, so it can span sittings.

phases.d: Draft a pilot, or bring a pre-made or made one.
Stop cards show the objective, clock, foes, gravity and weather.
A mission, an elite, a haven or an event.
Points, a trait offer, crystals, gear at a haven.
The last row; win, or Tumult keeps the expedition.

now.note: Seven rows in three acts, six mission kinds plus Elite and the Heart, havens, twelve events, a Lifeline, two tides.

plan.note: The atlas plan: a run is a random journey from one atlas page to another, joined by a story, with a tell-your-own mode later.

prop.note: Havens sell only gear (boons and consumables fold into it, P3), and the gear passives are the build-arounds the boons were.

holes.q: Win rates sit near 100% on most tier 1 and 2 missions for the look-ahead player, with the Heart at 25%, so the middle of an expedition carries little stake.
holes.fill: Tune the middle rows against the Gale and the Heart together, from node tools/sim.js 40, before adding content.

nodes.name: The draft
nodes.is: Make a pilot from human and two clades. The character workshop's first step.

phases.d: Packs drawn from the three pools; a trait you hold is never offered again.
Two cards awakened at least.
The pilot is kept on the device and, online, shared.

now.note: Draft, Quick Build of six pre-mades, made pilots kept and shared since 2.72; a canon question about the painted pilot.

plan.note: The dossier (design/06) asks for a backstory as the pilot is made.

holes.q: A draft shows card texts with up to 31 different state words, so a new player cannot see what a kit is for.
holes.fill: With 22 keywords (P2) the draft can show a pilot's keyword profile: three to five chips that say what it does.

nodes.name: The route
nodes.is: Choosing the next stop from the cards side by side.

now.note: Stop cards since 2.70 (objective, clock, foes, gravity, weather, bonus goals).

nodes.name: A haven
nodes.is: Rest, repair, buy and sell gear and consumables, train.

prop.note: Gear only. Each piece has two actives and one passive, so the shop is the build-around choice boons were.

nodes.name: An event
nodes.is: A narrative fork with two or three choices, costs and risks.

now.note: Twelve events; none repeats in a run.

prop.note: The Etherion Storm and Shrine hand out Affinities and boons today; they would hand out a gear passive or a trait instead.

nodes.name: Reward and train
nodes.is: After a won mission. Points, crystals, a trait for each pilot, a boon from an elite.

phases.n: Take a trait, or swap one in, or skip
Spend points on P or E

prop.note: Elites offer gear instead of a boon. A trait offer shows its keyword chips beside the pilot's, so a swap reads as a change of toys.

nodes.name: A mission
nodes.is: One objective on one atlas page. Every page names fifteen spaces, so every mission works on every page.

phases.d: The page, its gravity and weather, the objective and clock.
Usually 8 to 14.
A gold card on the board says what was done and how far along it is.
Bonus goals counted; a loss spends the Lifeline.
Plus 25% vitality; a canon question about the page.

holes.q: With no cards at all a squad still wins most missions, but kill missions are all but unwinnable (audit Pass C: the Heart 0%).
holes.fill: The basic Strike is the floor; under P2 a basic action may also Mark or Push, so a kill is never impossible.

nodes.name: A round
nodes.is: The puzzle. Foes have already said what they will do; the squad answers.

phases.d: Each foe declares, drawn as arrows and labels.
Track slides, engines fire, 4 dice into the bank (3 AP and 1 chosen element, planned).
Both pilots, interleaved, or one player at a time in Take turns.
A foe out of range closes instead; Hidden pilots leave afterimages.
Hazards, wind, Wounds, the clock, the objective.

now.note: The forecast says exactly what ending the round now costs (T.forecast).

plan.note: Dice rework: 3 AP dice and 1 element die of the player's choice each turn (Garrett, 2026-11-21).

holes.q: Two turns in five gave a pilot no real choice at 2.28 (41%, tools/turns.js). It has not been measured since four dice and the 2.73 balance pass.
holes.fill: Run node tools/turns.js 10 before and after the dice rework, and aim under 20% idle or forced turns.

nodes.name: A pilot's turn
nodes.is: Spending one pilot's AP and etherions on faces, steps, basic actions, gear and duets.

phases.d: AP, etherions, what is home on the track.
A setup and its payoff, yours or your partner's.
Channel a crystal, Brace, step.

prop.note: With 22 keywords (P2), every chain a turn can build is a pair of keywords from section 2 of the review doc; the hint bar can name the pair it sees.

nodes.name: A duet
nodes.is: One pilot sets up, the other cashes in. Spot, Leg up, Lend, and every face that buffs an ally.

phases.d: Mark, Weaken, Pull into range, a Field.

now.note: Duet moves since 2.28. Deterministic for the acting player, so a turn never waits on the partner.

prop.note: Link (P2) is the duet keyword that reaches across the board.

nodes.name: A face played
nodes.is: One card face, from choice to its card coming home.

phases.d: AP, plus etherions for an Ethereal face.
Deterministic; the numbers are the tooltip's.
Duration, then cooldown, then home. Once a turn at most.

prop.note: Every face says which line it is (body, magic, tech) by its keywords alone (P3).

nodes.name: Hover and see
nodes.is: Point at a face, die, token or intent; the game answers with numbers and a preview.

phases.n: The tooltip and the preview answer

now.note: Keyword chips with icons and one-sentence tips (src/ui/keywords.js), 29 of them.

holes.fill: A long press is the hover.

nodes.name: Swarm: hold the beacon
nodes.is: Waves arrive; a pilot near the beacon at round end counts a round held.

nodes.name: Vault: break in
nodes.is: A seal on a ledge, a lever and a ramp; height is the problem.

nodes.name: The Sought: find it
nodes.is: Hidden caches, one real, and Lurkers that ambush from Hidden.

nodes.name: Cascade: close the valve
nodes.is: A flood spreads every round; channel the valve before the clock ends.

nodes.name: Salvage: carry it home
nodes.is: Crates across the page, a round trip each.

nodes.name: Survey: tag the marks
nodes.is: Marks spread over the page; tag them all before the clock.

nodes.name: An elite
nodes.is: One tough foe with escorts; it offers a boon (gear, proposed) when beaten.

nodes.name: The Heart
nodes.is: Two phases; its shield is fed by Spawners, and at half the vault begins to drown.

nodes.name: A pilot grows
nodes.is: A made pilot comes home with its traits, points and level, and sets out again as it came home.

phases.n: Come home with traits and points

now.note: Since 2.76; missions scale to the pilot's level (docs/reference/SCALING.md).

plan.note: Design/06: the dossier records who the pilot is and what it did; three-pilot squads.

holes.q: The pilot keeps cards and points but nothing of what it did, so the workshop job stops at the build.
holes.fill: The dossier (P7): each expedition writes one line about the pilot from the faces it played and the canon its player wrote.

nodes.name: Canon from play
nodes.is: Players add or correct details of places, pilots, foes and events; each answer becomes a canon record for approval.

phases.n: A question at a pause, or a mark on a text

now.note: Marks on atlas, codex and events; questions after the draft and after a mission (docs/reference/CANON.md).

prop.note: A question names a keyword moment: "Your Pull dragged the Brute into the flood. What did the crowd shout?"

nodes.name: Playing with friends
nodes.is: The lobby, a code, or one screen at the table; one to five players, each flying their own pilot.

now.note: Lobby since 2.80, Take turns since 2.81, joining mid-route since 2.79.

nodes.name: The pilots' kits
nodes.is: The six pre-made pilots, each with its own loops. Pick one to make it the pilot shown everywhere in the atlas.

nodes.name: Releases
nodes.is: bleeding-edge to development (testers, the playtest page) to main (players). Rules and content change here.

now.note: Version bumps with every change; playtest NOTES rewritten each release.

holes.q: A player meeting a release learns of a new rule only by meeting it in play.
holes.fill: The title names what changed in keywords: "New: Link. Stasis now also stops movement."

nodes.name: The atlas grows
nodes.is: New pages of Tumult places, each grown from a Cosmic Shore pilot scene, each with its rules and field notes.

phases.n: Players meet it on the route

now.note: Nine pages (docs/reference/ATLAS.md); about 38 planetside scenes exist.

plan.note: Phases 2.18 to 2.23: zones, pages, gravity and weather, journey, tell your own, the full atlas in print.

nodes.name: On to the Cosmic Shore
nodes.is: A finished dossier is a pilot ready for the Hypersea; the fourth way onward is to leave Tumult.

plan.note: The proposed campaign ends where the Hypersea begins (design/01).

edges.why: Holding against waves trains for the Heart's called swarm.
An elite is a small Heart: one big telegraph to read.
The Heart's second phase drowns the vault.
A made pilot comes home with its traits and points.
A question about the page after each mission.
A question about the painted pilot while it is made.
A game in the lobby pulls you into a sitting.
A release brings new traits and pages.
The same pilot, a harder wind.
Points spent on P and E stay with a made pilot.
Approved canon becomes field notes and the storyteller pack.

free.name: Trying the kit
free.is: No objective. The Codex and the playtest jump, where a kit is tried for its own sake.

phases.n: Play one on a foe or the board

hold.name: A round holding the beacon
hold.is: Swarm: the kit spent keeping a pilot near the beacon while waves arrive. Area, Push and Shield pay here.

vault.name: A round breaking in
vault.is: Vault: the kit spent getting onto the ledge and working the lever. Height, Blink and Climb pay here.

phases.n: Climb, Blink or take the ramp

find.name: A round searching
find.is: Sought: the kit spent finding the real cache among the false ones while Lurkers wait. Reveal and Hidden pay here.

valve.name: A round against the flood
valve.is: Cascade: the kit spent reaching the valve and channelling it while the flood spreads. Hover, Haste and Cleanse pay here.

phases.n: See where the flood goes next

carry.name: A round of salvage
carry.is: Salvage: the kit spent carrying crates home, a round trip each. Move, Blink and Anchor (against the wind) pay here.

tag.name: A round of survey
tag.is: Survey: the kit spent tagging marks across the page. Reach, Move and Reveal pay here.

phases.n: Plan a line through the marks

fight.name: A round of battle
fight.is: Elite and the Heart: the kit spent on one tough foe and its escort. Mark, Empower, Pierce and Weaken pay here.

phases.n: Get out of it, or brace

roleHoles.q: Nothing measures which faces carry each kind of mission. The audit says where a face was played, not which round it decided.
roleHoles.fill: Add to tools/audit.js a count of the round each face moved the objective in, per mission kind, and show it on the pilot's Codex page.

kit.is: A pilot's nine traits at most, each with a Physical face (AP, scales with P) and an Ethereal face (AP and etherions, scales with E, played once the card has E 1), plus two gear. Shown here: the pre-made pilot's six.

holes.q: No pilot's combos are written down, so nothing checks that a kit teaches them or that a mission rewards them.
holes.fill: Each pilot names two combos: a feeder into a spender, and one that crosses two elements. The ones shown here are invented from the card texts for Garrett to correct.

pulse.name: Hover and see
pulse.is: Hover a face, a die, a token or an intent and the game answers with exact numbers and a preview on the board. The forecast says what ending the round now would cost.

phases.n: The tooltip and the preview answer

holes.q: On a phone there is no hover, so the pulse is missing there (roadmap P1).
holes.fill: A long press is the hover; the preview stays until the face is played or cancelled.

verbHole.q: This face's loop is written as what it does, not as steps, and the feeling it should give, and at which step, is not written.

phases: The state lands on the foe
You or your ally cash it in
setup.feel: Laying the ground the big hit will stand on.

burst.feel: A clean hit, exactly as large as promised.

reposition.feel: Changing the puzzle instead of answering it.

phases: The hit arrives smaller or not at all
ward.feel: Watching a promised hit come to nothing.

tap.feel: A clean decision, answered at once.

proposals.title: One ladder of words
proposals.what: Use the eight tier terms (Pulse, Verb, Combo, Round, Mission, Expedition, Arc, Era) in Tumult's design docs and reviews, the same ladder Cosmic Shore uses, so a problem is placed before it is argued.

proposals.title: Twenty-two keywords
proposals.what: Cut about 85 words of art to 22 keywords and a grammar of range and timing words. Field and Link are new; Wound and Hover reshaped; the rest merged. Every tooltip one sentence a player resolves by hand.

proposals.title: Body, magic, tech
proposals.what: Biophysical (Physical faces: you and beside you, now), bioethereal (Ethereal faces: any unit, at range, for N rounds) and ethereal technology (gear: spaces, dice, clock, the downed). Boons and consumables fold into gear passives and actives.

proposals.title: Every pilot names two combos
proposals.what: A feeder into a spender, and one that crosses two elements. The Codex and the hint bar teach them; the audit checks a mission rewards them.

proposals.title: Three AP and one chosen element
proposals.what: Each turn a pilot rolls 3 AP and picks 1 element; weak and refunding Ethereal faces cost 0 AP; stronger faces cost 2 or 3 etherions. Being built in its own thread.

proposals.title: The breath after an expedition
proposals.what: One question about the moment that mattered and one offered next step, instead of a return to the title.

proposals.title: The dossier writes itself
proposals.what: Each expedition adds one line to a made pilot's dossier, from the faces it played and the canon its player wrote.

proposals.title: Canon questions name a keyword moment
proposals.what: The game remembers the play that decided a mission (a Pull into a Field, a Link that felled two) and asks about that, so the player embellishes something the game gave.

Rosh.label: Rosh, the Brawler-in-the-Cloud

Mass.does: Melee 3, shove the foe 1, and recoil 1 node.
Mass.trigger: Ethereal face: 2 AP + 1 Mass (Physical Jet: Burst 2 in any direction.)
Mass.scales: At E 3: Melee 3, shove the foe 3, and recoil 1 node.

Charge.does: Point the mob at a foe within 3: it is Marked, your hits on it deal +1, and both heroes' next hit deals +1.
Charge.trigger: Ethereal face: 1 AP + 1 Charge (Physical Harry: Harry a foe within 2: it takes 3 and is Weakened 1 this round, and your ally's next hit deals +1.)
Charge.scales: At E 3: Point the mob at a foe within 3: it is Marked, your hits on it deal +2, and both heroes' next hit deals +2.

Space.does: Drop beside a foe within 3 and peck it for 3; if that leaves it at 2 hp or less, it falls.
Space.trigger: Ethereal face: 1 AP + 1 Space (Physical Circle Down: Circle down 2, over foes, and see everything beside where you land.)
Space.scales: At E 3: Drop beside a foe within 5 and peck it for 5; if that leaves it at 4 hp or less, it falls.

Time.does: Pre-arm: the next hit on you is reduced by 3. Dur 2.
Time.trigger: Ethereal face: 2 AP + 1 Time (Physical Read: Mark a foe: the next hit on it deals +2.)
Time.scales: At E 3: Pre-arm: the next hit on you is reduced by 7 and reflects 3 back. Dur 2.

Omni.does: A banked etherion no card wants becomes a basic action with no AP: Mass Strike or Shove, Charge Arc, Space Scramble, Time Brace.

Rosh.leanWhy: Closes through cover and drops on whatever is weakest.
